headline: 74 new obligations for plastic packaging makers, with no support to match.
body: The packaging regulation places 74 requirements and prohibitions on the companies that make plastic packaging. Not one support or funding measure is directed at them, even though 30 support measures across the legislation reach other sectors.

evidence.notes:
All three counts are taken across every row of all seven register files, attributing a row to a sector where the slug appears in sectors_named or sectors_reached.

74: rows touching chem/plastics whose derived valence is Requirement, Prohibition, Support cut or Entitlement withdrawn. All 74 sit in data/ppwr.json; no other register file carries a duty-side row for the sector. MIN-01, RCY-01 and BAN-01 are cited from that set as the minimisation duty, the recycled-content minimums and the Annex V format prohibitions.

Zero: no row typed 'incentive' anywhere in the register carries chem/plastics in sectors_named or sectors_reached, and no row touching the sector derives the valence Opportunity. The sector's entire favourable side is the five further cited rows -- FREE-03, REC-05, LAB-04, CNF-02 and EPR-04 -- three transitional or mutual-recognition rights, one conformity simplification and one procedural right. None of them moves an amount, a rate, an eligibility or the existence of any funding, which is what the incentive type requires; that is the sense in which the count is zero. Three further PPWR rows carry direction 'unchanged' and are counted on neither side.

30: rows typed 'incentive' anywhere in the register that carry at least one slug in sectors_named or sectors_reached -- iaa 16, ets 9, nzia 3, crma 2. Of the register's 39 incentive rows, 9 attach to no sector at all. The same 30 rows are returned by the stricter test of derived valence Opportunity, because the one incentive row typed as a Support cut is among the 9 that name and reach no sector. None of the 30 touches chem/plastics.
